# cgjrdata

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata)
<!-- badges: end -->

`cgjrdata` packages the indicators of the **World Bank Country Jobs and
Growth Report (CGJR)** institutional framework for the `cgjrapp` Shiny
dashboard. A hand-edited crosswalk maps each indicator to a leaf of the CGJR
taxonomy; the build joins that mapping onto the CLIAR data in
[`cliaretl`](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cliaretl) and ships
the result as long tables.

Closeness-to-Frontier (CTF) values are copied **unchanged** from `cliaretl`,
and an indicator is benchmarked only where CLIAR benchmarks it, so a country's
score on an indicator shared with the CLIAR app is identical in both apps.
cgjrapp computes every composite score live, from the member countries of the
selection.

The current data were built from `cliaretl`
`r attr(cgjr_ctf, "cliaretl_version")`.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cgjrdata")
```

You need a GitHub Personal Access Token with access to the
`WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop` organisation. `cliaretl` is needed only to rebuild
the data or to run the checks against it; using the shipped data does not
need it.

## Shipped objects

```{r objects, echo = FALSE}
objects <- list(cgjr_taxonomy = cgjr_taxonomy, cgjr_crosswalk = cgjr_crosswalk,
                cgjr_ctf = cgjr_ctf, cgjr_raw = cgjr_raw, wbcountries = wbcountries)
grain <- c(
  cgjr_taxonomy  = "one row per taxonomy leaf",
  cgjr_crosswalk = "indicator x leaf, annotated against cliaretl",
  cgjr_ctf       = "country x year x ctf_type x variable x leaf",
  cgjr_raw       = "country x year x variable x leaf (observed values only)",
  wbcountries    = "one row per country: region, income group"
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  object = paste0("`", names(objects), "`"),
  grain  = grain[names(objects)],
  rows   = format(vapply(objects, nrow, integer(1)), big.mark = ","),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

`cgjr_ctf` and `cgjr_raw` hold **real countries only** (`wbcountries`); World
Bank aggregates such as `AFE` or `WLD` are dropped. Region and income-group
comparisons are made from member countries using `wbcountries`. `year` is
`NA` for static CTF rows.

```r
# Kenya's dynamic CTF on the Degree of Integrity indicators
cgjr_ctf |>
  filter(unit_code == "KEN", ctf_type == "dynamic", leaf == "degree_of_integrity")
```

## Taxonomy and coverage

The taxonomy has `r n_distinct(cgjr_taxonomy$cluster)` clusters,
`r n_distinct(cgjr_taxonomy$subcluster)` subclusters and
`r nrow(cgjr_taxonomy)` leaves: Public Financial Management branches into four
sub-subclusters, and every other subcluster is its own leaf. Indicators per
leaf, and how many have dynamic CTF, static CTF and raw values:

```{r coverage, echo = FALSE}
cgjr_taxonomy |>
  mutate(leaf = coalesce(sub_subcluster, subcluster),
         leaf_name = coalesce(sub_subcluster_name, subcluster_name)) |>
  left_join(
    summarise(cgjr_crosswalk,
              indicators = n(), dynamic = sum(in_dynamic), static = sum(in_static),
              raw = sum(!is.na(raw_dataset)), .by = leaf),
    by = "leaf"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(indicators, dynamic, static, raw), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L))) |>
  select(cluster = cluster_name, leaf = leaf_name, indicators, dynamic, static, raw) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

`dynamic` and `static` count the indicators CLIAR benchmarks in that panel
(see `flag_ctf_eligibility()`). A leaf with no indicators yet has zeros.

Raw values come from these `cliaretl` datasets:

```{r sources, echo = FALSE}
cgjr_crosswalk |>
  count(raw_dataset = coalesce(raw_dataset, "(no variable yet)"), name = "indicators",
        sort = TRUE) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Rebuilding the data

The two CSVs in `data-raw/input/` are the only source of truth for the
taxonomy; see `data-raw/input/README.md`. After editing them, or after
updating `cliaretl`, run from the package root:

```r
source("data-raw/cgjr.R")   # rebuilds cgjr_taxonomy, cgjr_crosswalk, cgjr_ctf, cgjr_raw
devtools::test()            # data contract tests: every value equals cliaretl's
```

The build prints a checklist, a green ✔ for each check that passes:

```
✔ No duplicate taxonomy leaves.
✔ Every crosswalk row sits on a taxonomy leaf.
✔ Every variable is in the cliaretl catalogue.
✔ Every variable has CTF values in at least one panel.
✔ Every variable was found in a raw dataset.
✔ No duplicate observations on ctf_type / unit_code / year / variable / leaf.
✔ No duplicate observations on unit_code / year / variable / leaf.
```

A duplicate leaf, a crosswalk row off the taxonomy or a duplicate observation
stops the build (red ✖). A variable outside the `cliaretl` catalogue, without
CTF values, or found in no raw dataset only warns (!), because an indicator
may come from outside `cliaretl`.

`data-raw/wbcountries.R` rebuilds `wbcountries`; run it only when the World
Bank classification file changes.

## Exported functions

The build steps, exported so they are documented and tested:

| function | answers |
|---|---|
| `check_cgjr_mapping()` | Is the crosswalk consistent with the taxonomy and `cliaretl`? |
| `flag_ctf_eligibility()` | Does CLIAR benchmark this variable, dynamic and static? |
| `locate_raw_variables()` | Which dataset holds this variable's raw values? |
| `pivot_wide_to_long_cgjr()` | Wide country table to CGJR's long, labelled form. |
| `check_duplicate_obs()` | Does any observation appear twice? |

## Related packages

- [`cliaretl`](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cliaretl): the upstream CLIAR data
- [`cliarappak`](https://github.com/WB-PIDA-Data-Science-Shop/cliarappak): the CLIAR benchmarking dashboard
- `cgjrapp`: the CGJR dashboard that uses this package
